name: Ottoman ebru marbled paper
summary: Pigment floats on a thick bath of water. The marbler combs it into a pattern and lays a sheet on it for one monotype. Each sheet is unique, with flowing veins, combed curls and floral drops.

philosophy.core_thesis: A pattern that the water and the comb make together, and that no plate can repeat, gives a sheet of paper a living surface.
design_principles: Make each sheet as one pull: float the colours, comb them, then lay the paper on them.
Use 2–8 mineral and plant pigments, and float each one on the bath with a brush.
Draw with a stylus, a comb and a fan; keep the veins in smooth flowing curves.
Let a drop spread to a ring and add a smaller drop inside it, for a flower.
Use a ground of indigo, red or black and leave the veins in ochre, white and red.
Cut or frame the sheet as a border, an endpaper or a calligraphy margin.
Accept uneven colour density and a soft blur at the edge of each vein.
anti_patterns: A repeating tile or a mirrored pattern
A halftone dot or a photographic tone
Plate mark or relief in the paper
A uniform flat colour with no veins

process.matrix: A bath of thick water (size) that carries floating pigment. Ink floats and transfers flat, so the process is closest to planographic.
process.press: No press: the marbler lays a paper on the bath by hand, and the pigment transfers in one touch.
process.image_making: The marbler drops pigment on the size, then shapes it with a stylus, a comb or a fan.
process.edition: One sheet for each pull; no two sheets are the same.

inks.strategy: Several pigments that float on the size and do not mix; the ground and the drops come from the order of the drops.

screening.rule: There is no screen; make a tone with the density of floating pigment and with the spacing of the comb teeth, 2–5 mm apart.

registration.rule: One pull makes the whole sheet, so there is no register; a second pull for a frame can sit 1–2 mm off.

substrate.stock: A hand-made paper with a smooth, polished face (aharlı), treated with alum so that the pigment takes.
substrate.finish: Burnished and sized, ivory, with a smooth face.

surface.impression: No bite and no plate mark; the pigment lies as a thin film on the face.
surface.sheen: Matt, with a soft shine where the pigment is thick.
surface.texture: Smooth flowing veins with fine soft edges and small rings of colour.

marks: paper fibre that shows through thin colour

evidence.title: Diwan of Mehmed Raghib Pasha, a manuscript with marbled paper

lineage.root: Ebru comes from Persian and Central Asian marbling and from the Ottoman book arts; the data has no earlier print style of this kind.

emotion.target_response: Calm and wonder: the viewer sees a surface that moved like water and then stopped.

avoid_when: The image needs a precise repeat or a hard edge.
The design needs a figure or a readable scene.

modifiers.how: Replace the flowing veins with a drawn pattern on stone in 4–6 flat colours.
Cut the pattern in wood and print in one black ink.
